newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ex-president's top aide questioned in Colosio case.
newsitem.headline: Ex-president's top aide questioned in Colosio case.

text.p: Mexico's special prosecutor investigating the 1994 assassination of leading presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio has questioned a top aide of ex-President Carlos Salinas de Gortari, officials said on Friday.
Jose Cordoba Montoya, the right-hand man of Salinas during his 1988-1994 presidency, is one of the highest-ranking former government officials to be questioned in the case.
Salinas, who fled Mexico in disgrace after his brother was arrested in another political murder and now lives in Ireland, has not faced prosecutors' questions.

"Jose Cordoba Montoya appeared before the special prosecutor in his character as ex-chief of the office of the presidency of the republic to respond to an ample interrogation," the Attorney General's Office said in a statement.
The questioning took place on Wednesday, but officials waited two days to disclose it to the media.
Colosio, who almost certainly would have become president as candidate of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party, was shot at close range in the northern border city of Tijuana in March 1994.

The special prosecutor, Luis Raul Gonzalez Perez, is the fourth to take a crack at the case in two-and-a-half years. But so far only one man, confessed shooter Mario Aburto, has been convicted in the case, which the government inists was a conspiracy.
